description: A Python-embedded modeling language for convex optimization problems.

summary.what_it_does: CVXPY lets you write optimization problems using variables, objectives (Minimize/Maximize) and constraints in a form that follows the math, instead of the standard form solvers require. The README's example builds a bounded least-squares problem with cp.Variable, cp.sum_squares and a constraint on x. It lists numerical solver dependencies including Clarabel, OSQP, SCS, and HiGHS (highspy), plus NumPy and SciPy. The README points to a documentation site with a tutorial, an example library, and an API reference. It also links to a contributing guide, a Discord community, GitHub Discussions and Issues, and citation information for academic use.
use_cases: formulate least-squares and regression problems with bounds
model convex optimization problems in Python
prototype optimization models before choosing a solver
learn convex optimization with a tutorial and examples
how_to_run: Install CVXPY following the installation guide linked in the README (pip install cvxpy is the usual route; the README points to the guide rather than listing the command)
notable: Natural mathematical syntax for convex problems, not solver standard form
Multiple solver backends (Clarabel, OSQP, SCS, HiGHS) selected behind one modeling interface
Documentation, tutorial and example library hosted at cvxpy.org
Active community on Discord and GitHub Discussions
caveats: The README excerpt is truncated in the middle of the example code and the installation section, so exact install commands and some details are not visible
Minimum dependency versions are specified (e.g. NumPy >= 2.0.0, SciPy >= 1.13.0), which may constrain existing environments
The README says basic usage questions should go to StackOverflow rather than the issue tracker
